assumptions_and_boundaries.name: ascii_is_whitespace/ascii_trim_start_boundary/ascii_trim_start_index/ascii_trim_start_result
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: The harness reuses the audited shared ASCII whitespace and trim-start vocabulary. The formerly external choose/index bridge is now proved in the harness by establishing uniqueness of ascii_trim_start_boundary and then applying the choose witness property; this item no longer contributes a trusted proof boundary.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: u8::is_ascii_whitespace
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: The Rust target calls the primitive per-byte ASCII whitespace classifier. The harness preserves that observation through `byte_is_ascii_whitespace`, whose executable body matches the audited `ascii_is_whitespace` vocabulary, but does not recursively prove the primitive `u8` method body.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: trim_ascii_start leading first/rest split
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: Verus does not support the source `[first, rest @ ..]` slice pattern directly, so the harness mechanically lowers it to the same nonempty leading-byte branch using `bytes.len()`, `bytes.split_at(1)`, and `&head[0]` before assigning `bytes = rest` or breaking.

notes: The harness preserves the Rust 1.96 target flow: initialize `bytes = slice`, repeatedly inspect the leading byte, shorten to the rest while it is ASCII whitespace, break on the first non-whitespace byte, and return `bytes`. The target body contains no assume_specification, --no-verify marker, or target-body external_body. lemma_ascii_trim_start_index_matches_boundary is now a verified proof, not an external body.
